title: Slide a vegetable kebab off its skewer onto a plate with a fork: one hand holds the skewer, the other pushes
instruction: Take the vegetables off the kebab onto the plate with the fork: hold the skewer by its bare end and push the pieces off its point with the fork, then put the empty skewer down on the board beside the plate. Do not touch the vegetables with your grippers.
context: A kebab is served lying across a plate, and most people have taken one off its skewer at the table or the kebab-shop counter: hold the stick's bare end, push the pieces off its point with a fork, and set the bare stick aside. Recipes say it plainly: 'Use a fork to slide the vegetables off of the skewers.' It takes both hands because the pierced pieces grip the stick, about 1 N each, so the fork pushes about 4 N along a 3 mm, 10 g stick: a push that moves them drags a loose skewer across the plate with them, so one hand holds the skewer still against the fork while the other pushes. The fork has to stay just over the stick behind the last piece; set too high, it rides over a piece.
setup: Metres; x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the bench top; origin midway between the arm bases (0, +/-0.305). (1) A white dinner plate 260 mm across, floor 8 mm, rim wall 20 mm high, centred at (0.33, -0.16). (2) A vegetable kebab lies across it along y: a bamboo skewer 300 x 3 mm (Roland 71516), axis 26 mm up, centred at (0.34, -0.028), point toward -y at y = -0.178 (18 mm past the plate's centre), blunt end at y = +0.122, over the board beyond the rim; 10 g (a real one is about 2 g; see fidelity). On it from the point: a red bell pepper square 6 x 30 x 30 mm (6 g), a red onion block of three layers 18 x 25 x 30 mm (12 g), a courgette round 12 mm thick, 32 mm across (9 g) and a button mushroom, cap 35 mm across, 30 mm tall, flat side toward the blunt end (15 g), resting on the plate's floor; each pierced on the stick itself and held by a friction of 1 N along it (estimate; to measure; the sim leaves a 4 mm clearance outline). The run is 66 mm long, front face 40 mm and rear face 106 mm from the point; 194 mm of bare stick lies behind it. (3) A stainless dinner fork, IKEA FORNUFT, 190 mm (four tines 2.5 mm wide on 7.5 mm centres, head 25 mm, handle 3 mm thick widening from 7 to 16 mm, neck raised 8 mm; 45 g, estimate), lies on the board on its tines and handle end, neck at (0.10, -0.10), tines toward +x and -y, 35 degrees off x. Nothing else is on the bench. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Read at the end; only failures latch. A piece COUNTS when the fork (within about 2 cm of it) pushed it off the point while the skewer was held (both left finger pads within 4 mm of the bare stick, jaws shut to 6 mm or less, skewer within 30 mm of where it lay) and it now rests on the plate, inside 112 mm of its centre. Tiers: 0.25 the skewer is held by its bare end now, 1 s (a hand open over it does not count). 0.5 all four pieces count. 1.0 all four count and the bare skewer lies on the board off the plate (all of it outside the rim, under 12 mm up), still, both grippers 30 mm clear of the vegetables, for 2 s. Void (0): a gripper touches a vegetable (the whole gripper is read, 4 mm margin); a piece comes off the point without the fork pushing and the skewer held; a piece lands on the bench. Real trial: the top photo for the pieces and the skewer; the video for the hold, the fork and no gripper on a vegetable.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo reaches 1.0 at step 901 (45 s).
reset_notes: Nothing is random. Cut fresh pieces to the sizes above. Pierce each on the 3 mm skewer itself (or a 2.5 mm awl; no preformed 4 mm hole) for a friction grip. Check each slides on about 1 N: loop string round it, pull along the held skewer with a luggage or kitchen scale (replace if under 0.5 N or over 2 N). Set the run's rear face 106 mm from the point (66 mm run, front face 40 mm from it). Lay the kebab across the plate as above; wipe plate and fork. Blunt or cap the point to protect the pads.
fidelity: Pieces are rigid bodies of real size and mass on the stick by a sliding joint with a 1 N friction cap (estimate), removed when a piece's rear face passes the point; real pieces are pierced and soft. The stick is 10 g, not 2 g: a 2 g stick flicks when pinched. The fork is a rigid steel shape of the IKEA FORNUFT's size; its 45 g mass is an estimate. The 40 N pinch lets the stick drift about 15 mm under the push.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (no hold, nothing off the kebab in 1,200 steps). Demo: 1.0 (901 steps, 45 s, GPU). hold_only 0.25; no_aside 0.5; one_arm, fingers, offplate, hover, none 0.
failures: One arm pushes with the fork, skewer loose: the kebab slides across the plate with the pieces, nothing comes off, 0. Pieces pulled off by a gripper: void, 0. Kebab carried so its point is over the board: pieces land on the bench, void, 0. All four pushed onto the plate but the bare skewer left on the plate: 0.5.
